touches.text: There is no central supervisor. Each part starts what it needs by trying to use it: sending a message starts the bus if it is down, a message arriving wakes its shim, the shim wakes its device. Many very small supervisors, each one detect-and-start. WHY: a supervisor is one more thing to keep up, and the system must come up from any part that is touched.
The detect-and-start lives in one tool, the waker, and it sits inside connect: every client's connect is a wake attempt, so no caller can forget one. A probe watches and reports; the waker acts.

Two callers waking the same part at once start only one: the part that binds its socket first is the only one; a second copy finds it taken and exits quietly (as the ground loop does, 5.6.4.3). [Q#93: Ticket b38af5fd1852 says a second live copy of a host singleton refuses LOUDLY; this line says it exits QUIETLY. Your words, 2026-11-12: "when it's going to spin up another, the act of spinning it up should either exit or close the other. what needs to be a singleton per cairn? cairn itself across all boxes. maybe codemother. but on an individual host, that would be the ground loop, the bus, the rack, there can't be two akienasus_cc_0 on the same bus! that would be akienasus_cc_1". Two choices: the second copy exits (loud or quiet), or it closes the first (supersede). Is the answer the same for the bus, the ground loop, the rack and a device name?]

One bus per cairn instance, not per host. Each box runs its own bus, and the buses talk to one another, so a device always talks to the bus on its own box; together they are the instance's one bus. A device runs on one box; the other boxes reach it over the buses. No box needs a full set of devices. WHY: so the instance can run several heavy tasks at once across boxes.

Every box runs all the foundational things: a bus, a ground loop, the shims. They are the Cairn device's machines, and there is only one Cairn device: a singleton within the swarm, owning them on every box. WHY: Cairn is the system in aggregate, which is not the same thing as the host (6.6); a box is part of the host, and the swarm of boxes is still one Cairn.
